units.literal: The proper offices first fixed the honored posthumous title as Sagacious, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, Filial Emperor, with temple name Zhaozong—I dare say it overflows with praise and seems unlike straightforward writing.

units.zh: 今郊禋有日，祫祭惟時，將期允愜列聖之心，更在詳議新廟之稱，庶使葉先朝罪己之德，表聖上無私之明。」
units.en: The suburban sacrifice draws near and the collective ancestral rite is due; we must satisfy the former sages and deliberate anew the temple designation, that we may honor the late dynasty's virtue of self-reproach and display the present sovereign's impartial clarity."
units.literal: Now the suburban sacrifice has its day and the collective ancestral rite has its season; we will look to satisfy the hearts of the ranked sages, and further deliberate in detail the new temple designation, hoping thereby to accord with the late dynasty's virtue of blaming itself and display the present sage's impartial clarity."

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》云：蘇楷目不知書，僅能執筆，其文羅袞作也。）〉
units.en: (Old Book of Tang: Su Kai could scarcely read; he could barely hold a brush—his essays were written by Luo Gun.)〉
units.literal: (Old Book of Tang says: Su Kai's eyes did not know books; he could barely hold the brush—his texts were written by Luo Gun.)〉

units.zh: 太常卿張廷範奏議曰：「昭宗初實彰於聖德，後漸減於休明，致季述幽辱於前，茂貞劫幸於後，雖數拘厄運，亦道失始終。
units.en: Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Tingfan submitted: "Zhaozong at first showed true sagely virtue, but later his glory faded; Jishu kept him captive and Maozhen seized the imperial progress—though ill fortune pressed him repeatedly, he also lost the Way from first to last.
units.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Tingfan submitted a deliberation saying: "Emperor Zhaozong at first truly displayed sagely virtue, but later gradually diminished in glorious clarity, bringing Ji's seclusion and insult in front and Maozhen's seizing the imperial progress behind—though he several times met obstructed fortune, he also lost the Way in beginning and end.

units.zh: 違陵寢於西京，徙兆民於東洛，軔輦輅未逾於寒暑，行大事俄起於宮闈。
units.en: He abandoned the tombs in Chang'an, moved the people to Luoyang; scarcely a season passed before catastrophe struck within the palace.
units.literal: He departed from the imperial tombs in the Western Capital, moved the myriad people to Eastern Luo; the imperial carriage had not passed a season of cold and heat before great affairs suddenly arose in the palace women's quarters.

units.zh: 謹聞執事堅固之謂恭，亂而不損之謂靈，武而不遂之謂莊，在國逢難之謂閔，因事有功之謂襄。
units.en: I have heard that firmness is called Gong, surviving disorder unharmed is Ling, martial effort uncompleted is Zhuang, meeting national hardship is Min, and merit through events is Xiang.
units.literal: I have respectfully heard that firm solidity is called Gong, disorder without harm is called Ling, martial effort without completion is called Zhuang, meeting hardship in the state is called Min, and achievement through events is called Xiang.

units.zh: 今請改諡曰恭靈莊閔皇帝，廟號襄宗。」
units.en: I request the posthumous title Respectful, Spirited, Solemn, Sorrowful Emperor and the temple name Xiangzong."
units.literal: Now I request changing the posthumous title to Respectful, Spirited, Solemn, Sorrowful Emperor, with temple name Emperor Xiang."

units.zh: 輝王答詔曰：「勉依所奏，哀咽良深。」
units.en: Prince Hui replied, "I reluctantly follow your submission; my grief is profound."
units.literal: Prince Hui replied by edict: "I reluctantly follow what was submitted; my grief chokes deep."

units.zh: 楷附會幸災也如是。
units.en: Such was Kai's way of attaching himself to power and rejoicing in disaster.
units.literal: Thus did Kai attach himself to others' words and rejoice in disaster.

units.zh: 及梁祖即位於汴，楷自以遭遇千載一時，敬翔深鄙其行。
units.en: When the Liang Founder took the throne at Bian, Kai thought he had met a once-in-a-millennium chance; Jing Xiang despised his conduct.
units.literal: When the Liang Founder took the throne at Bian, Kai considered himself to have met a once-in-a-thousand-years moment; Jing Xiang deeply despised his conduct.

units.zh: 尋有詔云：「蘇楷、高貽休、蕭聞禮等，人才寢陋，不可塵穢班行，並勒歸田里。」
units.en: Soon an edict declared, "Su Kai, Gao Yixiu, Xiao Wenli, and others are base in talent and must not stain the court ranks—all are ordered home to their fields."
units.literal: Soon an edict said: "Su Kai, Gao Yixiu, Xiao Wenli, and others—their talent grows ever more base and cannot defile the court ranks; all are ordered to return to their fields."

units.zh: 循、楷既失所望，懼以前過獲罪，乃退歸河中依朱友謙。
units.en: Xun and Kai, disappointed in their hopes, feared punishment for past faults and withdrew to Hezhong to serve Zhu Youqian.
units.literal: Xun and Kai, having lost what they hoped for, feared punishment for former faults and therefore withdrew to Hezhong to rely on Zhu Youqian.

units.zh: 莊宗將即位於魏州，時百官多缺，乃求訪本朝衣冠，友謙令赴行台。
units.en: As Zhuangzong prepared to take the throne at Weizhou, many offices stood empty; he sought men of the old Tang gentry, and Youqian sent Xun to the mobile headquarters.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was about to take the throne at Weizhou, many offices among the hundred officials were vacant; he sought out gentry in official dress of this dynasty, and Youqian ordered them to go to the mobile headquarters.

units.zh: 時張承業未欲莊宗即尊位，諸將賓僚無敢讚成者，及循至，入衙城見府廨即拜，謂之拜殿。
units.en: Zhang Chengye did not yet wish Zhuangzong to assume the throne; none of the generals or staff dared approve. When Xun arrived he entered the headquarters, saw the offices, and bowed at once—this was called bowing to the hall.
units.literal: At the time Zhang Chengye did not yet wish Zhuangzong to assume the exalted throne; among generals and guest officials none dared praise and approve. When Xun arrived, he entered the yamen city, saw the commandery offices and at once bowed—this was called bowing to the hall.

units.zh: 時將吏未行蹈舞禮，及循朝謁，即呼萬歲舞抃，泣而稱臣，莊宗大悅。
units.en: The officers had not yet performed the court dance; at audience Xun cried "Long live the emperor," danced and clapped, wept, and declared himself a subject—Zhuangzong was delighted.
units.literal: At the time officers had not yet performed the treading-and-dancing rite; when Xun attended audience he at once cried "Ten thousand years," danced with clapping, wept and called himself subject—Emperor Zhuangzong was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 翌日，又獻大筆三十管，曰「畫日筆」，莊宗益喜。
units.en: The next day he presented thirty large brushes called "sun-painting brushes," and Zhuangzong was still more pleased.
units.literal: The next day he again presented thirty large brushes, calling them "sun-painting brushes," and Emperor Zhuangzong was still more pleased.

units.zh: 承業聞之怒，會盧汝弼卒，即令循守本官，代為副使。
units.en: Chengye heard and was furious; when Lu Rubi died, he had Xun keep his old post and replace him as deputy envoy.
units.literal: Chengye heard of it and was angry; it happened that Lu Rubi died, and he at once had Xun keep his original office and replace him as deputy envoy.

units.zh: 明年春，循因食蜜雪，傷寒而卒。
units.en: The following spring Xun ate chilled honeyed snow, took cold, and died.
units.literal: In the spring of the next year Xun, from eating honeyed snow, contracted cold damage and died.

units.zh: 同光二年，贈左僕射，以楷為員外郎。
units.en: In Tongguang year two he was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director, and Kai was named Vice Director.
units.literal: In the second year of Tongguang he was posthumously granted Left Vice Director, and Kai was made Vice Director.

units.zh: 天成中，累曆使幕，會執政欲糾其駁諡之罪，竟以憂慚而卒。
units.en: Under Tiancheng he served repeatedly in commissioners' staffs; when the authorities moved to prosecute him for rejecting Zhaozong's posthumous title, he died of shame and grief.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era he repeatedly served in commissioners' staffs; it happened that those in power wished to prosecute his crime of rejecting the posthumous title, and in the end he died of worry and shame.

units.zh: 史臣曰：昔武皇之樹霸基，莊宗之開帝業，皆旁求多士，用佐丕圖。
units.en: The historiographer writes: When the Martial Emperor laid the foundations of hegemony and Zhuangzong opened the imperial enterprise, both sought scholars broadly to assist their great designs.
units.literal: The historiographer says: In the past, when the Martial Emperor planted the foundation of hegemony and Emperor Zhuangzong opened the imperial enterprise, both broadly sought many scholars to assist their great designs.

units.zh: 故數君子者，或以書檄敏才，或以搢紳舊族，鹹登貴仕，諒亦宜哉！
units.en: These gentlemen, whether by nimble pen in letters and proclamations or by birth in old gentry families, all rose to high office—and rightly so!
units.literal: Therefore these several gentlemen, whether by nimble talent in letters and proclamations or by gentry of old clans, all ascended to exalted office—surely this was fitting!

units.zh: 唯蘇循讚梁祖之強禪，蘇楷駁昭宗之舊諡，士風臣節，豈若是乎！
units.en: Only Su Xun praised the Liang Founder's forced abdication and Su Kai rejected Zhaozong's posthumous title—can scholarly integrity and ministerial duty sink so low!
units.literal: Only Su Xun praised the Liang Founder's forced abdication and Su Kai rejected Emperor Zhaozong's old posthumous title—can scholar custom and ministerial integrity be like this!

units.zh: 斯蓋文苑之豺狼，儒林之荊棘也。
units.en: They are jackals and wolves in the grove of letters, thorns in the forest of scholars.
units.literal: These are jackals and wolves of the literary grove, thorns and brambles of the Confucian forest.

units.zh: 壬午，保義軍節度使朱友謙進百官衣二百副。
units.en: On renwu Zhu Youqian of the Baoyi Army offered two hundred sets of court robes.
units.literal: On renwu, Zhu Youqian, military governor of the Baoyi Army, presented two hundred sets of official robes.

units.zh: 五月，以唐朝宰臣張文蔚、楊涉並為門下侍郎、平章事；
units.en: In the fifth month former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
units.literal: In the fifth month, former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;

units.zh: 時霸府初開，幕客馬鬱、王緘，燕中名士，盡與之遊。
units.en: At that time the chief's headquarters had just been opened; the staff members Ma Yu and Wang Jian, both celebrated names from Yan, all associated with him.
units.literal: At that time the chief's headquarters had just been opened; the staff members Ma Yu and Wang Jian, both celebrated names from Yan, all associated with him.

units.zh: 及昭宗誅韓全誨等，左拾遺羅袞上言：「蕡當太和時，宦官始熾，因直言策請奪爵土，復掃除之役，遂罹譴逐，身死異土，六十餘年，正人義夫切齒飲泣。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong executed Han Quanhui and others, Left Reminder Luo Gun submitted words: "In the Taihe era, when eunuchs were just growing fierce, Fen in his straightforward examination answers asked to strip them of noble ranks and fiefs and restore the task of sweeping them away — thereby he suffered reprimand and exile and died in a foreign land; for more than sixty years upright men and men of righteousness gnashed their teeth and wept.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong executed Han Quanhui and others, Left Reminder Luo Gun submitted words: "When Fen was in the Taihe era, eunuchs were just growing fierce; because of his straightforward examination answers he asked to strip them of noble ranks and fiefs and restore the sweeping-away task — thereby he suffered reprimand and exile, died in a foreign land; for more than sixty years upright men and men of righteousness gnashed teeth and drank tears.

units.zh: 比陛下幽東內，幸西州，王室幾喪。
units.en: Compared with Your Majesty confined in the eastern inner quarters and fortunate to reach the western capital — the royal house nearly perished.
units.literal: Compared with Your Majesty confined in the eastern inner quarters, fortunate to reach the western capital — the royal house nearly perished.

units.zh: 使蕡策早用，則杜漸防萌，逆節可消，寧殷憂多難，遠及聖世耶！
units.en: If Fen's policy had been used early, gradual advance would have been blocked and sprouts prevented, rebellious conduct could have been eliminated — how could deep sorrow and many hardships extend so far as to reach a sage age!
units.literal: If Fen's policy had been used early, then gradual advance would have been blocked and sprouts prevented, rebellious conduct could have been eliminated — how could deep sorrow and many hardships extend so far as to reach a sage age!

units.zh: 今天地反正，枉魄憤胔，有望於陛下。」
units.en: Now Heaven and Earth have returned to correctness; wronged souls rage in their flesh — they look to Your Majesty."
units.literal: Now Heaven and Earth have returned to correctness; wronged souls rage in their flesh — they look to Your Majesty."

units.zh: 帝令史建瑭以輕騎嘗寇，獲芻牧者二百人，問其兵數，精兵七萬。
units.en: He sent Shi Jiantang with light horse to scout, took two hundred foragers, and learned that the enemy elite alone numbered seventy thousand.
units.literal: The Emperor ordered Shi Jiantang with light cavalry to probe the enemy; he seized two hundred foragers and asked their strength—they said the elite numbered seventy thousand.

units.zh: 詰旦，進軍，距柏鄉一舍，周德威、史建瑭率蕃落勁騎以挑戰，四面馳射，梁軍閉壁不出，乃退。
units.en: At dawn he moved up to within one march of Baixiang; Dewei and Jiantang led tough frontier horse in circling challenges and volleys until the Liang men shut their walls and would not fight, then drew off.
units.literal: At dawn he advanced, halting one stage from Baixiang; Zhou Dewei and Shi Jiantang led fierce frontier cavalry to challenge, riding about on four sides shooting; the Liang army shut their walls and would not come out, and they withdrew.

units.zh: 十二月丁巳朔，梁祖聞帝軍屯趙州，命寧國軍節度使王景仁為北面行營招討使，韓為副，相州刺史李思安為前鋒，會魏州之兵以討王鎔；
units.en: On dingsi, the first day of the twelfth month, learning that the Jin host lay at Zhao, the Liang Founder made Wang Jingren of Ningguo overall northern commander, with Han as his deputy and Li Si'an of Xiang as vanguard, to unite Wei forces against Wang Rong;
units.literal: Twelfth month, first day dingsi, the Liang Founder heard that the Emperor's army was encamped at Zhao and appointed Ningguo Army military commissioner Wang Jingren overall northern campaign commander, with Han as deputy and Xiangzhou prefect Li Si'an as vanguard, to join Wei troops and attack Wang Rong;

units.zh: 時鎮州王熔、定州王處直叛，結連晉人，故遣將討之。
units.en: Wang Rong of Zhenzhou and Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou had rebelled and joined the Jin, so troops were sent against them.
units.literal: At the time Zhenzhou’s Wang Rong and Dingzhou’s Wang Chuzhi had rebelled and allied with the Jin, so generals were sent to attack them.

units.zh: 矧又王熔、處直未曾削爵除名，若翻然改圖，不遠而復，必仍舊貫，當保前功。
units.en: Wang Rong and Chuzhi have not been stripped of rank; if they turn back soon, they keep their posts and their past merit.
units.literal: Moreover Wang Rong and Chuzhi have not yet been stripped of rank and name—if they turn back and return not far off, they shall keep their old posts and preserve their former merit.

units.zh: 成汭，淮西人。
units.en: Cheng Rui came from west of the Huai.
units.literal: Cheng Rui was a native of Huai West.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》云：入蔡賊中，為賊帥假子，更姓名為郭禹。）〉
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says he joined the Cai rebels as an adopted son and renamed himself Guo Yu.)〉
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: entering Cai rebel bands, he became a rebel chief's adoptive son and changed his name to Guo Yu.)〉

units.zh: 少年任俠，乘醉殺人，為仇家所捕，因落發為僧，冒姓郭氏。
units.en: As a young man he killed someone in a drunken brawl, was hunted by the victim's kin, shaved his head as a monk, and took the surname Guo.
units.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and bold, killed a man while drunk, was seized by the enemy family, and therefore shaved his head to become a monk and usurped the surname Guo.

units.zh: 汭嘗仇殺人，懼為吏所捕，改姓郭氏。
units.en: After a feud killing he had taken the surname Guo to evade the law.
units.literal: Rui once killed in feud; fearing capture by officers, changed surname to Guo.

units.zh: 後據歸州，招集流亡，練士伍，得兵千餘人，沿流以襲荊南，遂據其地。
units.en: He took Guizhou, rallied refugees into a thousand-man force, sailed downriver against Jingnan, and seized it.
units.literal: Later he seized Guizhou, gathered fugitives, drilled soldiers, obtained more than a thousand troops, along the river struck Jingnan, and thus held that territory.

units.zh: 唐僖宗朝，為蔡州軍校，領本郡兵戍荊南，帥以其凶暴，欲害之，遂棄本軍奔於秭歸。
units.en: Under Xizong he was a Caizhou officer garrisoning Jingnan until his commander, fearing his violence, tried to kill him; he fled to Zigui with his troops.
units.literal: In Emperor Xizong's Tang he was a Cai prefecture army officer, led the prefecture's troops to garrison Jingnan; the commander because of his ferocity wished to harm him, so he abandoned his army and fled to Zigui.

units.zh: 初，澧、朗二州，本屬荊南，乾寧中，為土豪雷滿所據。
units.en: Li and Lang, once part of Jingnan, fell to the local strongman Lei Man in Qianning.
units.literal: At first Li and Lang two prefectures originally belonged to Jingnan; in Qianning they were held by local strongman Lei Man.

units.zh: 天祐三年夏，太祖以汭歿於王事，上表於唐帝，請為汭立廟於荊門，優詔可之。
units.en: Tianyou 3, summer: the Founder had the Tang court approve a temple for Rui at Jingmen, honoring his death in service.
units.literal: In summer of Tianyou year 3 the Founder because Rui died in royal service memorialized the Tang emperor requesting a temple for Rui at Jingmen; gracious edict approved.

units.zh: 亡匿久之，及貴，方復本姓。
units.en: He lived in hiding for years and only restored his true name once he had risen.
units.literal: He hid in flight a long time; when he reached eminence he then restored his original surname.

units.zh: 及為荊南節度使，命準為表，乞歸本姓。
units.en: As Jingnan commissioner he had Zhun draft a memorial to restore the name Cheng.
units.literal: When he became Jingnan military commissioner, ordered Zhun to draft a memorial begging restoration of original surname.

units.zh: 又云：「成為本姓，郭乃冒稱。
units.en: It added, "Cheng is my true name; Guo was a borrowed lie.
units.literal: Also said: "Cheng is the original surname; Guo is usurped claim.

units.zh: 伏乞聖慈，許歸本姓」云云。
units.en: I kneel and beg Your Majesty to let me bear my true name again," and so on.
units.literal: Kneeling beg sacred kindness, permit restoration of original surname," etc.

units.zh: 累官至檢校太尉，封上穀郡王。
units.en: He rose to honorary Grand Commandant and was made Prince of Shanggu.
units.literal: In succession he reached honorary Grand General and was enfeoffed Prince of Shanggu commandery.

units.zh: 楊行密以兵圍鄂州，汭出師以援鄂，淮寇乘之，以火焚其艦，汭投江而死。
units.en: When Yang Xingmi besieged Ezhou, Rui sailed to relieve it; the Huainan fleet burned his ships and he drowned himself in the river.
units.literal: Yang Xingmi with troops besieged Ezhou; Rui marched out to relieve E; Huainan raiders seized the moment, used fire to burn his warships; Rui threw himself in the river and died.

units.zh: 未至夏口，汭敗溺死，淮人遂陷鄂州，洪為其所擒，被害於廣陵市，時唐天復二年也。
units.en: Rui drowned in defeat before Xiakou; the Huainan army took Ezhou, seized Hong, and executed him at Guangling market in Tianfu 2.
units.literal: Before reaching Xiakou, Rui was defeated and drowned; Huainan men then took Ezhou; Hong was captured by them, killed at Guangling market—then Tang Tianfu year 2.

units.zh: 汭性豪暴，事皆意斷，又好自矜伐，騁辯淩人，深為識者所鄙。
units.en: Rui was domineering, arrogant in debate, and widely scorned by men of judgment.
units.literal: Rui's nature was arrogant and violent; affairs were all decided by his own intent; he also loved self-praise, vaunted eloquence to overbear others, and was deeply despised by the knowing.

units.zh: 一夕，巨蛇繞其身，幾至於殞，乃祝曰：「苟有所負，死生惟命。」
units.en: One night a giant snake coiled around him until he nearly died; he prayed, "If I am guilty, let fate decide."
units.literal: One night a huge serpent coiled around his body, almost to his death; he then prayed, saying: "If I bear some guilt, life and death are fate's alone."

units.zh: 是時荊州經巨盜之後，居民才一十七家，汭撫輯凋殘，勵精為理，通商訓農，勤於惠養，比及末年，僅及萬戶。
units.en: Jingzhou after the great devastations held only seventeen households; Rui rebuilt trade and agriculture until, by his last years, the city neared ten thousand families.
units.literal: At that time Jingzhou after great bandits had only seventeen resident households; Rui pacified the devastated ruin, strove in governance, opened commerce and trained farming, diligently in nurturing kindness—by his last years barely reaching ten thousand households.

units.zh: 汭奏請割隸，唐宰相徐彥若執而不行，汭由是銜之。
units.en: Rui asked the court to annex them; Chancellor Xu Yanruo refused, and Rui nursed a grudge.
units.literal: Rui memorialized requesting to detach and subordinate them; Tang chancellor Xu Yanruo held firm and did not carry it out; Rui thereby harbored resentment.

units.zh: 及彥若出鎮南海，路過江陵，汭雖加延接，而猶怏怏。
units.en: When Yanruo passed Jiangling en route to his Nanhai post, Rui received him coldly despite the courtesies.
units.literal: When Yanruo went out to command Nanhai, passing Jiangling, Rui though adding courtesies was still displeased.

units.zh: 汭赧然而屈。
units.en: Rui flushed and fell silent.
units.literal: Rui blushed and was subdued.

units.zh: 成汭鎮荊南，辟為推官。
units.en: When Cheng Rui held Jingnan he made Zhun his investigating officer.
units.literal: Cheng Rui garrisoned Jingnan and recruited him as investigating officer.

units.zh: 後因汭生辰，淮南楊行密遣使致禮幣之外，仍貺《初學記》一部。
units.en: On Rui's birthday Yang Xingmi sent gifts from Huainan—and added a copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.
units.literal: Later because of Rui's birthday Huainan Yang Xingmi sent envoys with ceremonial gifts besides, still bestowing one copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.

units.zh: 準忿然以為不可，謂汭曰：「夫《初學記》，蓋訓童之書爾，今敵國交聘，以此書為貺，得非相輕之甚耶！
units.en: Zhun was furious and told Rui, "The 《Elementary Studies》 is a schoolbook for children. An enemy state sends it as a state gift—is that not open contempt?
units.literal: Zhun angrily deemed it unacceptable, told Rui: "The 《Elementary Studies》 is merely a book for instructing children; now enemy states exchange missions—using this book as a gift, is it not extreme mutual slight!

units.zh: 汭不納，準自歎曰：「若然，見輕敵國，足彰幕府之無人也。
units.en: Rui refused. Zhun sighed, "Accept this and we show the enemy our staff has no one with spine.
units.literal: Rui did not accept; Zhun sighed to himself: "If so, being slighted by the enemy state sufficiently shows the headquarters has no men.

units.zh: 汭怒其去，潛使人於途中殺之。）〉
units.en: Rui, enraged, had him murdered on the road home.)〉
units.literal: Rui angry at his departure, secretly sent men on the road to kill him.)〉

units.zh: 太祖命荊南成汭率荊、襄舟師以赴之。
units.en: The Founder ordered Cheng Rui of Jingnan to sail the Jing-Xiang fleet to his aid.
units.literal: The Founder ordered Jingnan Cheng Rui to lead Jing and Xiang river fleets to go relieve.

units.zh: 及成汭敗於鄂州，匡凝表其弟匡明為荊南留後。
units.en: After Cheng Rui fell at Ezhou, Kuangning had his brother Kuangming made acting Jingnan commissioner.
units.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated at E prefecture, Kuangning memorialized his younger brother Kuangming as Jingnan acting commissioner.

units.zh: 成汭之敗，其兄匡凝表為荊南留後。
units.en: After Cheng Rui's defeat his brother made him acting Jingnan commissioner.
units.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated, his elder brother Kuangning memorialized him as Jingnan acting commissioner.

units.zh: 乙太府卿敬翔知崇政院，翔與帷幄之謀，故首擢焉。
units.en: Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang was put in charge of the Chongzhengyuan—first among promotions because he had shared the Emperor's counsels in the field.
units.literal: Appointing Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang to oversee the Chongzhengyuan; Xiang had shared in secret planning within the tent, hence he was first promoted.

units.zh: 可改唐天祐四年為開平元年，國號大樑。
units.en: Let Tang's Tianyou year 4 become Kaiping year 1; the realm shall be called Great Liang.
units.literal: Let the fourth year of Tang's Tianyou be changed to the first year of Kaiping; the state name is Great Liang.

units.zh: 是夜，莊宗令於軍中求憲，或曰：「與王緘俱歿矣！」
units.en: That night Zhuangzong ordered a search for Xian in the army; someone said, "He perished together with Wang Jian!"
units.literal: That night Zhuangzong ordered a search for Xian in the army; someone said, "He perished together with Wang Jian!"

units.zh: 十五年，王師戰胡柳，周德威軍不利，憲與同列奔馬北渡；
units.en: In the fifteenth year the imperial army fought at Huliu; Zhou Dewei's army fared ill, and Xian fled north across the river with his colleagues on horseback;
units.literal: In the fifteenth year the imperial army fought at Huliu; Zhou Dewei's army fared ill, and Xian fled north across the river with his colleagues on horseback;

units.zh: 暇日游豫至焦梨店，頗述前事，念王重榮舊功，下詔褒獎而封崇之。
units.en: At leisure he visited Jiaoli Shop, spoke of old days, and remembering Wang Chongrong’s service issued praise and enfeoffment.
units.literal: In leisure he traveled for pleasure to Jiaoli Shop and, recalling earlier events, thought of Wang Chongrong’s old achievements—he issued an edict of praise and enfeoffment.
